author: Dakota Times
title: Vikings place center Ryan Kelly on injured reserve ahead of Lions matchup
text:
Kevin O'Connell, Head Coach at Minnesota Vikings | https://www.vikings.com/
Kevin O'Connell, Head Coach at Minnesota Vikings | https://www.vikings.com/
The Minnesota Vikings have placed veteran center Ryan Kelly on Injured Reserve (IR) for the second time this season, the team announced Wednesday. This move comes just before their Week 17 matchup against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium.
Kelly left Sunday's game after entering concussion protocol, despite using a Guardian Cap helmet cover designed to provide additional protection. It marked his third entry into concussion protocol during the 2025 season.
Earlier in the year, Kelly first encountered a concussion during Minnesota’s Week 2 home opener against the Atlanta Falcons, leaving after 23 snaps and returning in Week 4 against Pittsburgh in Dublin. He suffered another concussion in that game and was again sidelined on IR before returning to play in Week 12 at Green Bay.
The four-time Pro Bowler and former first-round pick by the Colts had contributed significantly during December, aiding Minnesota’s undefeated record for the month prior to exiting last Sunday’s contest after 21 snaps. His placement on IR means his debut season with Minnesota is limited to eight games.
"Michael Jurgens is expected to start in Kelly's place against the Lions," according to team sources. Jurgens, selected in the seventh round of the 2024 draft, has played in 16 games over two seasons and previously started in Week 3.
Minnesota also promoted interior offensive lineman Henry Byrd from its practice squad to fill out its active roster. Byrd has participated in two games this year but only on special teams.
Linebacker Sione Takitaki was elevated from the practice squad via standard elevation rules after making his debut for Minnesota on special teams last week against New York Giants. Additionally, rookie tight end Gavin Bartholomew has been downgraded from questionable to out due to an ongoing back injury within his evaluation period.
The Vikings will wear their Winter Warrior uniforms for Tuesday's "Winter Whiteout" game against Detroit as part of a tradition where fans are encouraged to wear white at U.S. Bank Stadium.
